---
title: "nmaplot test"
output: html_notebook
---

```{r packages}
library(netmeta)
library(nmaplots)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 10, fig.height = 10.5, dpi = 150)
```

```{r data}
data(mash)
d <- mash$fib_improvement_alldoses
```

```{r network}
p <- pairwise(treat = treatment, event = responders, n = sampleSize,
              studlab = study, data = d, sm = "RR")

net <- netmeta(p, reference.group = "Placebo")

nmaplot(net, outcome = "Fibrosis improvement without worsening of MASH")
```

```{r ring}
# outer ring from the design column of the data (RCT / PSM)
nmaplot(net, ring = table(d$treatment, d$design), ring_name = "Study design",
        outcome = "Fibrosis improvement without worsening of MASH")
```

```{r save}
nmaplot(net, ring = table(d$treatment, d$design), ring_name = "Study design",
        outcome = "Fibrosis improvement without worsening of MASH",
        file = c("mash_net_graph.png", "mash_net_graph.pdf", "mash_net_graph.tiff"),
        width = 10, height = 10.5, dpi = 300)
```

```{r layouts}
nmaplot(net, ring = table(d$treatment, d$design), ring_name = "Study design",
        outcome = "Fibrosis improvement without worsening of MASH", layout = "circle")
nmaplot(net, ring = table(d$treatment, d$design), ring_name = "Study design",
        outcome = "Fibrosis improvement without worsening of MASH", layout = "star")
```

```{r defante, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 10.5, dpi = 150, out.width = "100%"}
# nmaplot() is laid out for a ~10 x 10.5 in page: text sizes are fixed in
# points, so a smaller figure squeezes the network under the labels. The chunk
# options above set that size for the notebook preview; maximising the output
# window only enlarges the bitmap. For the Plots pane use
# "Chunk Output in Console" (gear icon), where the plot is redrawn on resize.
unloadNamespace("nmaplots")
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("vanioljantunes/nmaplots")
library(netmeta)
library(nmaplots)
library(readxl)


myfile <- rstudioapi::selectFile()

# take sheet names from excel file selected
  sheet_names <- excel_sheets(myfile)

  # create a list called ma where the data sets will be saved and named according sheet names
  ma <- lapply(sheet_names, function(x) {as.data.frame(read_excel(myfile, sheet = x))})

  # name the objects inside the list with the sheet names
  names(ma) <- sheet_names
  
  d <- ma$rec_pat
p <- meta::pairwise(treat = treatment, event = responders, n = sampleSize,
              studlab = study, data = d, sm = "RR")
net <- netmeta(p)

# Same input as netgraph(net). Title is centred; the outcome becomes the subtitle.
nmaplot(net, outcome = "X")

# Outer ring from a column of the data: one label per study arm, counted per
# treatment. Here study design (RCT / PSM), but any categorical column works.
nmaplot(net, ring = table(d$treatment, d$design), ring_name = "Study design",
        outcome = "Fibrosis improvement without worsening of MASH")
```
